units.source_text: 此诗及刘禹锡诗，皆根据宋玉《高唐赋》中语：

en.t: This poem and Liu Yuxi's poem are both based on words from Song Yu's Gao Tang Fu:

units.source_text: “昔者，先王尝游高唐，怠而昼寝，

en.t: In ancient times, the former king once visited Gao Tang; tired, he slept during the day,

units.source_text: 梦见一妇人，曰：‘妾巫山之女也，

en.t: and in a dream he saw a woman, who said: 'I am a woman of Mount Wu,

units.source_text: 为高唐之客，闻君游高唐，愿荐枕席。’

en.t: a guest at Gao Tang. Hearing that you have come to Gao Tang, I wish to offer you my pillow and mat.'

units.source_text: 去而辞曰：‘妾在巫山之阳，高丘之岨，

en.t: When she left, she took her leave and said: 'I dwell on the sunny side of Mount Wu, on the steep slope of a high hill;
at dawn I become morning clouds, and at dusk I become passing rain.
Morning after morning and evening after evening, I am beneath the Terrace of Yang.'
The next morning he looked, and it was just as she had said.'
